open_points.subject: K-16 vs M28 `service_instances`
open_points.text: K-16: "An installation selects one manifest instance per service"; M28: "service_instances: at most one selected instance per service ... a service with none selected is not invocable"
open_points.question: Is selecting an instance mandatory for every service, or may a service have no selected instance?
options: Exactly one selected instance is required per service
Zero-or-one selected instance is allowed per service; none means not invocable
Exactly one is required only for services that appear in accepted bindings/active flows
open_points.default_guess: Zero-or-one is allowed, and invocation is refused when none is selected.

open_points.subject: M19 Run status when waiting and execution coexist
open_points.text: "While some nodes wait, independent branches keep running (K-09)." and "status ... `running`, `awaiting_approval`, `pending` ... a run may wait at several nodes at once — its status is `awaiting_approval` when any of them waits for the owner's approval, otherwise `pending`"
open_points.question: What single run `status` must be stored when some branches are still executing and at least one waiting point exists?
options: Keep `running` until no node is actively executing
Set `awaiting_approval`/`pending` whenever any waiting point exists, even if other branches are still running
Disallow this overlap and force scheduler behavior so it cannot occur
open_points.default_guess: Use waiting-priority status (`awaiting_approval` else `pending`) whenever any waiting point exists.

open_points.subject: M19 Run terminal rule with failures plus unresolved waits
open_points.text: "The run is `failed` when no node can run any more and some node failed"; also runs can rest `awaiting_approval`/`pending` and "No wait ends by itself" (K-09).
open_points.question: If a run has a failed node and also unresolved waiting points, when does it become final `failed` versus remain waiting for owner actions?
options: End `failed` as soon as no runnable node remains, regardless of waiting points
Remain waiting while any waiting point exists; only finalize after waits are resolved/refused/cancelled
Differentiate by dependency (finalize only if all waits are on branches that can no longer affect outcomes)
open_points.default_guess: Finalize as `failed` when no runnable node remains, even if waiting points are still present.

open_points.subject: M22 SpooledFile read action
open_points.text: M22: "read by ... the owner's inspection read of its bytes (A10 rule 2; the State 5 operation `read_spooled_file`)" while State 0 primary actions list only "inspect ... typed description" and does not list `read_spooled_file`.
open_points.question: Which product action reads spooled file bytes, and is it part of the State 0 surface or a later addition?
options: Treat byte reading as part of existing `inspect` action
No byte-read action; only metadata is readable

open_points.subject: M10 ManifestOperation identity across instance-address changes
open_points.text: M10 includes `base_url`/`required_headers` from the selected instance, but identity evidence says: "equal readings of the same record digest are the same. Continuity: none; a changed record is another reading."
open_points.question: If selected instance address/headers change without changing the operation record digest, is that a new ManifestOperation fact for lifecycle/reads, or the same one?
options: It is a new ManifestOperation reading because invocation facts changed
It is the same ManifestOperation as long as `record_digest` is unchanged
Such instance changes are disallowed without restart/rebinding
open_points.default_guess: Treat changed instance address/headers as a new ManifestOperation reading used by subsequent actions.

open_points.subject: Binding actions when no instance is selected
open_points.text: M28 says "a service with none selected is not invocable"; M10 says manifest reading is used "when a binding is proposed or accepted and every time the operation is invoked".
open_points.question: Are `propose binding` and `accept binding` allowed for a service that currently has no selected instance?
options: Allow propose/accept; only invocation is blocked
Refuse propose/accept until an instance is selected
Allow propose but refuse accept until an instance is selected
open_points.default_guess: Allow propose/accept based on manifest operation record; block only invocation.
